about.title: Oceanside Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Oceanside sits at the northern edge of San Diego County, and its roads carry a mix of commuters, beachgoers, and military traffic every day. In 2025, the city recorded 835 injury collisions, with 1,177 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Public records show crashes are most often reported on Route 76, Oceanside Boulevard, College Boulevard, and Mission Avenue, and they tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. as the week winds down. If one of those collisions involved you, the next few weeks matter. Medical bills arrive before the insurance questions are answered, and the other driver's adjuster may call sooner than you expect. We handle Oceanside car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you may still pursue compensation even if you shared some blame, so a quick brush-off from an insurer is not the last word.

items.title: Deadlines are tracked from day one
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or public roadway defect is involved, a claim may need to be filed within six months. Our team will identify which deadline applies to your Oceanside crash.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. We can push back when an insurer tries to assign you more blame than the evidence supports.

items.title: Evidence gets preserved before it disappears
items.desc: Dashcam footage, skid marks on Oceanside Boulevard, and witness memories fade quickly. We move early to secure records and advise you not to give the other insurer a recorded statement until you have counsel.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to wait until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks to argue you were partly at fault or not seriously hurt. A brief, polite decline is enough while you get legal counsel.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Route 76 in Oceanside during Friday evening traffic. What should I do now?
items.answer: Start by getting checked by a doctor, even if you feel mostly fine, because soft-tissue and head injuries often show up later. Keep photos of the vehicles, the exchange of information, and any police or CHP report number. From there, our team can review your case at no upfront cost.

items.question: Can I still recover if I was partly to blame for the collision?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility instead of being barred entirely. Insurers know this and sometimes overstate your share, so having an attorney review the evidence can matter. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case.
